newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends flat after volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends flat after volatile trade.

text.p: Brazil's real closed steady at 1.0615 to the dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after a volatile session, dealers said.
In the morning, the local currency traded between 1.0600 and 1.0613 reais.
After noon, dollar demand caused the real to fall to 1.0616 prompting the Central Bank to sell dollars to the market, dealers said.

Although Tuesday's preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a $50 million surplus, dealers said net dollar flows would likely show another deficit when all transactions were registered. On Monday, forex contracts posted a $183.3 million deficit.

The market continued divided about the next decline in the reais-dollar mini-band. Some dealers are now expecting a change in the mini-band on Wednesday, before the four-day Eastern holiday. But others don't expect the Central Bank to move before Monday.

The current mini-band was set March 17 between 1.0565 and 1.0615 to the dollar. So far this month, the mini-band has been lowered 0.52 percent. In the last few months, the mini-band was lowered between 0.55 percent and 0.65 percent.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real closed steady at 1.0621 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 0.90 percent to end at 1.125 to the greenback.
